change: Reuse completed direct grouped rate-family ratios with delayed metadata removal.
proof: Direct GroupedSubquery demand, reserved-metadata-eliminating Float/single-head group plans, exact clocks, unique pair certification and separate successful group/binary completion. Prefix and global binary delayed guards remain.
implementation: Compile-time allowance specializations preserve ordinary entry arguments; existing runtime grouped+delayed proof selects the extension. No new retained state or raw history cache.

qualification.original_reuse: Fresh authenticated pinned captures made for candidate1, reused unchanged for candidate2.
qualification.static: Strict default/fixture lint, format, installed MSRV1.91 compile-only.

memory.scope: Accounted finite-query ownership; category peaks are not additive or process RSS. Early observations exact; other category peaks/current ownership do not grow.

cost_review: Immediate, relative and cumulative fixed executable costs reviewed under66, separately from query memory. No architecture-specific throughput inference.

previous_candidate.reason_for_revision: Actual shared entry gained a runtime allowance argument/instructions. Const specialization isolates the compiled variants; this does not establish a causal explanation for whole-query timing.
previous_candidate.policy: Same corpus, resource gates and timing thresholds; new candidate bytes, no unchanged retries or threshold relaxation.

scope_limits: Finite synthetic same-input qualification, not universal equivalence.
Timing targets use server-default options plus explicit delayed flag; controls include early mode and delayed fallbacks.
Strict whole-row ordering failures remain failures; the agreed deterministic-order policy is reported separately.
No live-dbengine, concurrent-query, process-RSS or physical ARM throughput claim.
Native/multiple-head, metadata-retaining, raw-selector-pair, mapped/prefix and nested delayed ratios retain existing fallback.
